Review Text: This is an impressive sparkling, under the BdB banner, but it feels like it delivers much more weight if one had in mind some BdB styles out there to compare that command more of a light/chalky/citrus frame. This wine has a ripe bouquet, verging on some light tropical notes. There’s lemon curd, yellow apple, mango swirl, peanut brittle. But also a refreshing lift of brine and preserved lemon. Then, a hit of sweetness in the middle with a pithy, chewy finish of a lime sorbet. It has fine mousse, silky texture and no shortage of flavour. It’s quite intense, both on the nose and on the palate and thus admirable in that sense. I was a bit overwhelmed at first, but rewarding the bold style and intensity here. If you know J&S Fielke still Chardonnays, you will recognise the style under the bubbles. Definitely one to try.

Author: Kasia Sobiesiak
Wine / Article: KT + Peglidis: Celebrating 20 Years – The Peglidis Vineyard Watervale Riesling Collection 2007-2026
Review Text:
This tasting was a deep dive into a great story of a vineyard farmed by passionate humans, Bunny and Ivonne Peglidis, since 1970. They are now 93 and 85 years old and not even thinking of putting down the secateurs. Since 2006, Kerri Thompson has been creating compelling wines from these now 56-year-old Riesling vines. Gary and I tasted the wines and their evolution over 20 years.

More preamble, ie a couple of remarks. No matter how you look at it, the wines across the board showed great quality. I have given plenty of 93-95s. Felt a bit boring, but this mirrored, for me, the overall great consistency in quality coming from this vineyard and the winery. Yes, there are better and worse vintages, but no crazy dramatic dips or misses; rather, a diversity, a vintage variation reflected in the wine’s profile. All are individual wines telling different stories, but with a common thread of complexity and texture.

Preamble 2: It’s great to taste a line-up like this. Normal thing to taste at pace at an event; first quick impressions are good, but I can imagine looking at these wines with time in the glass and over a few days, again and again, and those scores would potentially shift by 1-2 up or down, but that’s really the spread.

[Vintage notes from KT]
[All wines marked as 12%, only 2007 marked as 12,5%]

2007 12,5%
Mid-January rainfall provided relief from a warm, dry season, producing concentrated fruit & generous flavour.

KS: Deep golden colour. Lemon slice and a milk lolly quality. Development in full swing, but the acidity, albeit soft, feels very fresh. Beeswax, honey cake, even a note of cold brew coffee, herbs and more wax, preserved lemon in brine. Moving into smoky, peaty-almost notes. The apogee of what you’d like to taste in an aged Riesling; maybe it’s an indulgence just for a glass but a sensory treat. 94 points, drink now
GW: Rich, honey, Bickfords lime, toast, mint, even some spice. It’s a richer style showing plenty of development but it still has a fresh line of juicy acidity through it and finishes well.  A bit of lime marmalade too. Lovely wine. Still has some cellaring potential but likely at peak now. 94 points

2008
Defined by early, compressed ripening and a dramatic late-season heatwave.

KS: Some development here, but lots of freshness too. Wet slate, a vegetal, earthy edge, very savoury profile, led by citrus, maybe a hint of green papaya skin and orange pith. Super zingy, slate-y acidity to close. A curious disparity between this and 2007, only a year difference, but more lush development in 2007. Both tasty. 93 points
GW: Quite a tangy expression, a bit jangly, some hay-like character through lemon drops and lime. Sort of nutty with a citrus zest finish of good length. A little bit chalky in texture. Not quite the length but interesting and no hurry. 91 points

2009
Cooler conditions delivered elegance, tension and natural acidity.

KS: Flint and sweet citrus, oregano, dusty hay, wild peach. Lemon blossom, chalky palate that grips upfront. Crunchy green apple and jasmine, delicate and pure but impactful. Impressive and so fresh still. 95+ points
GW: Juicy but has tight acidity, lemon lime, a bit richer sort of a halfway house between 2007 and 2008. It’s a little spicy and dusty. A sherbet tang and a bit of grip on a finish of excellent length. Impressive. Has a bit of a burst to it. 95 points

2010
Generally even ripening conditions created wines of balance, freshness and longevity.

KS: Waxy citrus skins, crushed slate, mango skin, almond blossom, then smoked almond perhaps and candle wax. Acidity is cool and calm, but a bit broader than 2009, with a pink grapefruit finish. Just feels a little hollow in the middle, but it’s a good wine. 93 points
GW: Sits a little flatter and rounder in the palate, a light chalky feel, old orange flavours, some lime, with a nutty finish of solid length. Good drink. Very ready. 91-92 points

2011
One of the coolest and wettest vintages on record, with only one in three bunches ultimately picked.

KS: Sweet tones, with a ripe durian edge, and a vegetal sweetness, grapefruit and cucumber. It opens up with air into lemon lolly, frangipani perfume, and feels a touch musky. It has a deep flavour midway, just a bit less tension in that line than in some previous wines. 94 points
GW: A more apricot and cumquat character here, kind of exotic but I like the Germanic feel and some hessian complexity, and it drinks really well, but the point of difference is a really good thing. Like it. Tasty. 93ish points

2012
Benchmark Clare Valley mild conditions produced wines of purity and expression.

KS: Milk lolly creamy quality, lemon curd, creamed honey. Palate is broad in a way but spread evenly, with plenty of flavour, mostly light and flinty-salty on the palate. A bit warmer in the aftertaste, but it has something interesting going on, lightness but impact too. 94 points
GW: Ansieed riding very high, caraway, ripe lime with an exotic touch. Its very juicy and flavoursome, covers the mouth with flavour but in a gentle way, finishes limey and long. A superb wine,. Pleasure zone now nut no hurry. 95 -96 points

2013
Warm conditions delivered flavour intensity and early appeal.

KS: Green orange, smoked lemon, sage, fleshy citrus, pithy, a bit nervy flow, energetic. Some more papaya at play, with a salty finish. Brisk wine. 93 points
GW: Cut fennel, fresh mango, lime, a floral note. It has quite a bit of chalky powdery grip, a core of cool acidity, and impeccable length. This is so delicious with texture a bit of a highlight. A zesty tang on exit. Great. Love this. 95 points

2014
Warm, dry conditions followed by relieving mid-February rains and cool nights made for excellent fruit concentration.

KS: Rather quiet, restrained start, mostly citrus-led, developing into blossoms, gentle flow, lemon flower, almonds, savoury flinty nuance, lime sorbet vibes, with a very smooth, silky palate. Pretty wine. 94 points
GW: A slight petrol note, not a thing but the first time noted in the wine. A bit of hessian, fresh pineapple and lime, a light grip, with a rounder more waxy finish. 91-92 points

2015
Dry conditions produced wines of depth and structure.

KS: A bit musky perfume, sugar almond, parsley root, cool flow of flavour. Green fennel, pickle brine, salty and sweet-sour in a good way, à la green mango. No huge tension here, relaxed in style. 94 points
GW: Fennel, a little tropical, ripe lime, floral. It’s fresh, has some grip, a fleshy feel, almost a glycerol touch, with a spicy finish of good length. Very nice. 94 points

2016
Balanced growing conditions delivered exceptional varietal expression and purity.

KS: Apples, peaches and hot rocks, flint, lift and tension on the nose, very linear, bolt of lightning acidity, very pure citrus, slice of lemon on tongue, bitter lime finish. Very much wet slate texture. Pure and racy. 95 points
GW: Caraway, spice, lime, some floral things. It’s dry, a bit tangy, with a quite tight acidity, lime pith on a finish of good length. More to come. 93-94+ points

2017
Cool conditions favoured finesse, tension and longevity.

KS: Fresh start, green mango, lemon curd, golden kiwi, crushed slate. Raw nuts and herbs, smoky element. Very vivid and crunchy, slippery and youthful for its age. Pure and lifted. Has a lot of potential energy. 95+ points
GW: A bit of perfume here, lemon barley, lemon zest, leaf and mint, a little spice, a smoky touch. Lighter style, almost peppery, citrus, a kiss of sweetness rounds out a charming and different vintage for this wine. 94 points

2018
Warm, dry, low-yielding season delivered width, generosity and early appeal.

KS: It feels heavier than 2018, richer; mango, orange, hint of apricot stone, herbed honey, acidity is ripe but has a salty finish for a good balance, just a bit shallow here and there but it’s still a good wine. 92 points
GW: A more tangy lime zest and lemon affair, peanut butter, white flower. Acidity is a bit bitey but it does have intensity, and a lemon biscuit finish of good length. 92 points

2019
Dry conditions and smaller crops produced intense fruit concentration.

KS: Very concentrated from sniff to sip. Honey cake, lemon tart, apple tart, add a baked lemon. Seems very ripe/baked, but it’s of a style, and the palate has a huge concentration of acidity and comes with a big swoosh. There’s so much mid-palate weight here. Stony texture with wet chalk finish. This reminds me of a Germanic late harvest European style. Even though it’s delicious, it may feel at its capacity of development, so perhaps drink now/soon. 96 points
GW: This has the fruit volume turned up. Green mango, lime, spice, lime leaf. It’s intense and tight in the mouth, a chalky grip, almost a lime pickle intensity on a finish of excellent length. Very good. Could do with a bit more time as some rugged character to it, but good makings. Very good. 95 points

2020
Difficult season marked by drought conditions and exceptionally small crops.

KS: Quite concentrated at first, mirabelle plum, golden mango, softer and sweeter than 2019, also broader, and a bit loose and with a bitter lime in the back end. A tad clunky (tough gig when measured against its vintage peers). 92 points
GW: A fleshy wine, sits a bit flat, ripe lime, a light grip to texture, a rounder style with less energy than some but it’s still a nice drink. 89-90 points

2021
Near-perfect growing conditions produced wines of elegance, detail and remarkable balance.

KS: Smoked fruit, water on hot rocks, slate and salt, jasmine and lemongrass. Beautiful fabric of acidity, tight but so smooth, flowing with ease. Firm peach, peach blossom, green apple, and that note petrichor tone – the wet slate thing following through. Eyewatering acidity will allow it to age. 95+ points
GW: Perfumed, lemon/lime, a bit stony. It’s tight, very chalky, lots of lemon like, a good bite to it, with very good length. Good energy. Excellent. 95 points

2022
Cool, dry weather through summer and into autumn provided favourable ripening conditions, producing fruit with good natural acid levels and varietal flavour.

KS: Green mango skin, lemon lolly, lime cake and a flinty tension. Great acidity, very high, tickled my nose, watered my mouth. Nervy tension with salt. Good one. 94+ points
GW: Quite perfumed, vanilla bean and white flowers, white peach and lime, Japanese ginger. A more juicy experience, a lightness to it, and spice, with a light chalky grip and a grin and tonic finish of good length. Nice. 94 points

2023
Cool conditions encouraged purity and aromatic lift.

KS: Something nutty, musky up first, dusty/compact powder note, a bit of ripe tropical skin like durian; then more sweet citrus, mandarin, pomelo, sweet and briny-pickly flavours. The texture is pithy and phenolic, with bitter-sweet citrus peaking up in the finish. Peculiar but good. 95 points
GW: Green banana, lemon barley, lime, dried herb and lime leaf. It’s grainy, has a grapefruit tang to acidity, a good burst of flavour with a limey finish of very good length, again some quinine bite. Like it. 94 points

2024
Balanced season produced wines of brightness and energy.

KS: Love the perfume, fennel in brine, quite herbal wine, with raw almond and pear; it’s a bit closed at first, but gives a really beautiful pure fruity flow. The finish is pleasantly bitter and with salt over lemon. It has an X factor; can’t name it, that’s what the X factor is… 95+ points
GW: A softer and finer style, lemon and lime, a powdery feel to texture, some lime juiciness, with a zesty finish of good length. Very nice. In evolution, of course. 94+ points

2025
Dry conditions delivered smaller crops with flavour concentration and drive.

KS: Bright yellow in the glass. It smells like lemons, lemon sorbet, yellow apples, peach. It’s a very pretty wine, plenty of concentration. Stony texture, salty, and a bit chewy. 95+ points
GW: Lime, lemon, stony, a bit of of a mint and leaf perfume. It’s tangy, some tonic water, a chalky thing, quite some energy, a zesty and slightly rugged finish, but a wine of excellent character and intensity. 94+ points

2026
A complex season with significantly diverse weather patterns. A cool Spring then warm, dry Summer, followed by late season harvest rain.

KS: Very fresh and estery and yeasty, a bit lychee and kiwi and grape juice, with ginger spice. Super fresh aromatics, mint and blossoms. It’s a bit hard to see now, steaming cake straight from the oven; let it cool, give it time. Has the bones. 94+ points
GW: Highly perfumed, green ginger, fresh lime and lemon. It’s fresh, on the cusp of ripeness, but has a certain sort of energy, with a light herbal tang, a salted lime finish of good length. I like it. 94+ points.

This is a new one for J&S Fielke, and it’s only fair to make a quick note on how it stacks up against the Lenswood Chardonnay 2025. Things come in abundance in this wine but with certain grace and purity. Red apples, almonds, firm nectarines and oats. It has intensity and concentration but with a tight line of acidity, and a notion of coolness in the fruit profile. Beyond this, there’s a note of shortbread, a whiff of white chocolate and flint, with plenty of balancing bitter citrus. The texture is smooth, peach yoghurt-like, with a tingling ginger spice in the long finish. Elegant, lifted and fine. Another steal.

Author: Kasia Sobiesiak
Review Text:
Almost every day, before or after I taste wines, or just before or after I post the reviews, I run a conversation in my head about the objectivity of things and the silliness of the work that I do, but in fact love doing. It’s a dialogue, perhaps; I take into account all the arguments about tasting wines blind, to remove any bias, but then actually how to tell the story if it’s all blind, because isn’t the context the most important thing about wine? The people, the place, the motive? Anyway, I think I just wanted it to be known that I go through this every single time: the duality of things, the existential crisis of a tortured wine taster trapped in a material world trying to communicate the spiritual (don’t pity me, it’s a cool job). So, about this wine, I pondered on it, in the ‘biased context’ over two days. I actually do that with many of the wines that I taste: give them time, give them air, second chance, trying to understand the background and what the artist wanted to communicate… Rant over.

Day 1: First up, a whack of black olive tapenade; there’s definitely a vibration of green olive here too, leafy-stemmy notes (fully destemmed wine) and a woody bitterness. It has some compelling perfume that changes and improves with air exposure and time, but it’s quite a sour-savoury expression, perhaps a bit lean and feels ‘bunchy’, although it’s not. I’m baffled. 89 points

Day 2: Given a second day chance, as it was bothering me. Still peculiar. Lots of savoury, slightly vegetal tones, wet forest, moss on stones, fresh woody spice, pine needle resin, dark amaro bitterness; this can be a difficult wine, edgy, moody, quinine-driven. But now, it’s intriguing, compelling. Has a character and made me stop; this must count for something in the AI era. Maybe needed time. Who doesn’t. 92 points

Review Text:
Just noticed, Mount Henry’s climbing up the premium price tag ladder. In this rhythm, next year it will be double its 2021/23 price. Shiraz in Pinot disguise. Seemingly light and delicate, but it has depth and concentration. Beautiful, vibrant colour and perfume. Sweet forest berries, raspberries, some blue, some black too. Aromas are bright, with light shining through, but flavours are dark, deep and spicy. It’s a sunny day in a damp forest. There’s wet bark, rose potpourri here, cherry wood, mint tea, black liquorice, and a medicinal edge to it all, with a bit of iron-like aftertaste. I feel the detail is coming in with time, with air. Let it be in the glass, give it time and say what you will, these two can go together very well, the Shiraz and the Pinot Noir.

Author: Kasia Sobiesiak
Wine / Article: Yangarra High Sands Grenache: Celebrating 15 Vintages (2010-2024) [Nov25]
Review Text:
I have no words except the ones I wrote a few days ago. Peter’s voice is still saved in my phone’s recordings file. I transcribed some of it. I wasn’t sure whether to post this or not, but perhaps my reflections from this very special tasting can serve as a tribute. It was a true privilege to taste with Peter this very last time. Here’s what I wrote and was about to post this morning.

My dad used to collect rocks and had (still has) a pretty amazing knowledge of minerals and precious stones. We often ventured to the Sudeten Mountains in the Lower Silesian district of Poland to dig in the white mud, the kaolin clay. Such fun! We’d find different types of quartz, agate, chrysoprase, tourmaline, pyrite… As a teenager, I remember browsing through the miniature rock collection at home and memorising the astral-sounding names. Little did I know that one day I’d be collecting rocks in a liquid form, or at least, what I’d like to think is a liquid interpretation of the terroir. Such fun!

What I tasted at the Celebration of 15 Vintages of Yangarra’s High Sands Grenache was a true collection of gems. Some shining bright, some a bit more rough and perhaps fading, but all equally precious. It was very interesting to see the vintage variation in the glass, but also clear to note that the soil sets the foundation, literally and metaphorically, for the high quality—seen across the board. It’s important to know that High Sands vineyard is not simply white sand dunes. As Peter Fraser explained, “The [High Sands] vineyard sits in the Maslin sands geology, which is not to be confused with sand [per se]. That references the red ironstone, which lies beneath those vineyards. You’re going to go on the hill and see that red ironstone, and you’ll see it in various pockets where it’s at the surface. Highly ferrous, got that real red colour, and often you’ll see those little sand grain kind of characters. Above that sits the clay layer, which is orangey red because of the ferrous nature of the bedrock that influences that clay. So the water passing across it basically releases all of that mineral. And then in these various pockets, there aren’t that many of the Grenache vineyards that are actually really white sands.”

Among the 15 vintages, Peter identified four distinct seasons and weather patterns, indicating a variety of corresponding styles. The vintage groupings were presented as follows.

Cold and wet vintages
2011 cold and wet
2017 just cold
2020 odd one because it was a lower crop from a hot spring but then it was cold
2022 another odd one, cold vintage with a heat spike (looks warm but has tightness, hence held back)
2023 was very cold, maybe the coldest ever, with a low crop

Mild, classical vintages
2010, 2012, 2013, 2016, 2021 was cooler of the mild ones

Warm with low crop vintages
2015, 2019, 2025 perhaps

Hot vintages with a generous crop
As Peter described, “[…] they tend to have that lush, much juicier kind of palate, but also can be still really fragrant and look a bit lighter because of that slightly elevated crop.”
2014, 2018, 2024

2010
The colour is intact, very vibrant, deep ruby with just a light brick hue at the very rim. Tertiary development in full force in the form of soft, aromatic leather, roasted coffee bean, rose potpourri, and roasted sage leaf. It shows concentration and density on the palate, remnants of cherry-scented oak. Tannins are rocky, dark, dusty, fine pumice stone, more of an iodine/sage extract in the finish and a ripe, mature pomegranate juice acidity line. This is to drink now, but in great shape. 95 points

2011
Feels a bit muted/subdued on the nose. This has a lighter, more ethereal and translucent profile than the 2010. The wine has a very clear acidic tension, which is the first thing that hits the palate. It’s tight and lean, skeletal a bit in a way, and hence, oddly, doesn’t really show its age. It does come across a bit anemic and fading. There’s a cherry menthol lolly here, some red fruit. Nothing wrong with it, good for a glass or a couple of sips. It crossed my mind that it may be a sleeper, but it didn’t show lots of energy per se. This is probably the weakest link in the whole lineup. 89 points

2012
Again, a darker appearance than the previous vintage, deep ruby core. And as expected, it smells of dark fruit, mulberry and black cherry, black raspberry, elegant oak, cedar and dark chocolate, with cherry smoke. Plenty of flavour, juicy, meaty, chewy tannins. This is a big boi. Smoked plum and plenty of spice in the finish, it’s all dark and fibrous, charry in a good way. Start drinking now. 95 points

2013
This also shows great concentration and density on the eye and the nose, roasted coffee bean, a hint of Bonox, very ripe, drying fruit, and cherry pip. Big flavour, juicy, sweet-sour, cherry cinnamon and cola root, black liquorice, it’s almost black current themed. With a heap of fine puckering tannins borrowed from the Nebbiolo department. It feels like this still has room to develop. 96 points

2014
Ripe perfume, but with lifted strawberry and red cherry. Very fine stony tannins, dark slate to feel, and a pomegranate finish. Juicy and translucent on the palate, seemingly light, but in fact, it has a great presence and packs a punch. Plenty of liquorice, red and black, with exotic spice, musk. Very admirable. And long. Solid. 96 points

2015
Aromatic summer berries, mulberry, and boysenberry. There’s ripeness here and great concentration, really running deep. The acid line is ripe but long and built around wet chalky, fine clay texture. Peppery spice builds up in the aftertaste. This impresses and satisfies. 95 points

2016
This has a blueish/bruised hue. And what comes on the nose is bloody, cool, fresh, meaty, with the perfume of violets and salty black liquorice. The palate is velvety too, with blue damson plum, mulberry, cool acidity, something like a tobacco leaf too and bitter cold brew in the finish, chewy alpine herbs. Delightful. 96 points

2017
A bit lighter in appearance than its predecessors. Very pretty, floral, with almond and orange blossom lift, tarragon and roses, very fine detail in the perfume, wild strawberry, blueberry. Fine, lacy web of tannins. Super lovely wine, but it seems a little less concentrated than 2016. It’s just a bit more fruity and easier on the palate with a leaner tannin muscle. Drinking very well now (for Pinot drinkers). 94 points

2018
Pure deep ruby colour, violet rim. Cool perfume, raspberry, mulberry, roses. Some exotic spice in the mix, too, cinnamon, star anise. The flavour is very energetic, great balance of acid and tannin. Drinking with ease, very approachable. It delivers the concentrations upfront, but then the flavour splashes out and disappears a bit early. Delivers a great first impression, even if slightly more watery in the back end. Juicy, fruity, chewy. Drink now. 94 points

2019
Very red fruited to start with. Juicy, well-balanced, not overly tense or tannic, a bit loose to the finish, but delivers a very pleasing combo of sweet fruit, spice, chewiness, red liquorice. Tannins linger, but the flavour dissipates a bit on the way. 93 points

2020
The perfume is serious; none of that tutti-frutti. It’s all savoury, potpourri, meat, dried blood, bitter herbs, spice. Very concentrated and long, spicy, dense, velvety texture, it has a ripe sweet-salty core, very much black liquorice, amaretti biscuits, glossy cherry, but it’s savoury-bitter on the outside with wet clay tannins, and chewy spice. Powerful, delicious. Great wine. 97 points

2021
Deep ruby, purple reflections. Tense, lifted, cool nose, full of blue fruit perfume and a ripe red fruit base, a note of alpine amaro, violet, orange peel, blood orange bitter-sweet acidity. This is a beautiful drink, all classy, fine, pretty, high tones, great acid, long finish. 97 points

2022
Wow, what a vibrant, ruby colour, with a purple hue and hot pink edge. Almost the same is the perfume, vibrant, electric. Acidity is through the roof, carrying fine, squeaky tannin; the palate is like chewing on the bitter-sweet-sour skins of red plums and blackberries. Powerful with acidity as a highlight for sure will allow it to live long. 96+ points

2023
Jasmine green tea perfume. Lovely. Roses and violets, red fruit, red apple skin. It feels more Pinot-esque in a way. Approachable tannin profile, juicy, fruity, very pretty. For Pinot drinkers. Acidity is very perky, frisky, white chalk-like, lots of finesse here, fine detail, prettiness. 95 points

I scored it 96-97 on previous (early) tastings; this time around landed on 95, but probably somewhere between that and 96.

2024
This wine has 10% whole bunch. Beautiful translucent violet colour. Freshly picked strawberries with the tops on. Perfumed, orange blossom, almond blossom, wet tobacco leaf, or wet green tea leaf, jasmine. A bit of bresaola, green peppercorn. The palate is like hibiscus tea, or stewed rhubarb, that light red fruit brew, peppery spice, crushed bitter herbs, chalky palate. This is a good wine with an aromatic green edge, so if you’re not fond of it in wine, you may not love it. It has fine detail but is a bit loose in the back end. Very Pinot-esque, super pretty. However, it’s still early days. Release in May 2026. 93+ points (for now)
